title: Docsbook Skill Frontmatter
description: JSON Schema for the YAML frontmatter of a SKILL.md file in the docs-skills catalog.

description.description: Short human-readable description used for discovery and AI matching.

mode.description: What the skill is allowed to do to the docs. `audit` reports and changes nothing. `refactor` rewrites existing pages, preserving meaning, and never creates new ones. `authoring` is a rule set loaded BEFORE new writing, and never repairs old pages. `platform` configures the workspace itself rather than the content. The three content modes are mutually exclusive on purpose: a skill that both audits and rewrites cannot be trusted to do either.

requires_docsbook_mcp.description: True only for skills that genuinely need the Docsbook platform (e.g. workspace configuration, webhooks). Analysis/read skills must NOT set this — they state a need and work on any docs folder; declare optional accelerators via `accelerated_by` instead.

accelerated_by.description: Optional, NON-gating list of tools that make the skill faster/cheaper when connected (e.g. markdown-lsp, docsbook-mcp). The skill still works without them via plain file reads / grep / find. Entries are bare tool names; inline YAML comments are allowed.

requires_plan.description: Minimum Docsbook plan required to use this skill. `business` is the tier that unlocks webhook registration (canRegisterWebhooks in the product's plan-capabilities), bring-your-own API keys, UTM analytics and retention cohorts. A skill that registers a webhook needs it; claiming `pro` there walks a paying customer into a refusal they cannot act on.

uses_mcp_tools.description: List of Docsbook MCP tool names the skill calls.

produces_files.description: Files the skill writes or modifies in the user's repo.

output_schema.description: URL of a JSON Schema the skill's machine-readable output conforms to.

pipeline_subagents.description: Names of pinned subagents this skill orchestrates, in pipeline order.

keywords.description: Discovery keywords used by find_skill matching.

measures.description: Metric ids from metrics/metric-dictionary.json that this skill interprets. Reference the dictionary instead of restating what a metric means in prose — the meaning, its confounders and the metrics it must be read alongside are defined once there.

metric_dictionary.description: Relative path to the metric dictionary this skill reads (usually ../../../metrics/metric-dictionary.json).
